papers.title: Spatial control of mitochondrial ubiquitination by the AMBRA1-RMC1-HUWE1 axis.
papers.summary: Mitochondrial ubiquitination drives quality control, but how it proceeds without Parkin was unclear. The authors describe an AMBRA1 scaffold where RMC1 recruits the E3 ligase HUWE1 to mitochondria, promoting ubiquitination and turnover of outer-membrane proteins MFN2, VDAC1, and VDAC2—a Parkin-independent route raising questions about how cells choose among ubiquitination pathways.

papers.title: Marked for destruction? When S-nitrosylation writes protein fate through metabolic rewiring.
papers.summary: Loss of the denitrosylase AKR1A1 increases S-nitrosylation, impairing glycolysis and driving methylglyoxal accumulation, which carbonyl-modifies KEAP1 and targets it for selective autophagic degradation. The authors propose glycation as a metabolic "mark" for selective autophagy, and suggest that clearing metabolically modified proteins can sustain signaling supporting tumor progression and therapy resistance.

papers.title: Upstream regulatory mechanisms and clinical significance of IQGAP2 deficiency in affecting PI3K activity to drive cell proliferation.
papers.summary: IQGAP2 deficiency drives aberrant proliferation, but upstream mechanisms were unclear. Knockdown enhanced PI3K activity within the IQGAP1 complex, raising PIP3 and activating AKT/mTORC1, alongside Wnt/beta-catenin and AREG/EREG-EGFR signaling. Pan-cancer TCGA analysis shows the IQGAP1/IQGAP2 ratio is elevated in tumors and marks poor survival, suggesting a prognostic biomarker.

papers.title: Cross-population QTL mapping and association analysis identify breeding-ready markers for high seed protein content in elite soybean accession HJ117.
papers.summary: QTL mapping and GWAS across two soybean recombinant inbred populations from high-protein accession HJ117 (52.99% protein) identified nine stable loci—three major ones on chromosomes 15 and 20 explaining up to 41.5% of variance—plus 168 significant SNPs including a breeding-ready marker. Candidate genes GmSWEET10, GmSOP20, and POWR1 implicate sugar transport in seed protein accumulation.

papers.title: Argonaute protein and small RNA expression patterns in Spodoptera frugiperda (Lepidoptera, Noctuidae).
papers.summary: Characterizing piRNA pathways in the fall armyworm Spodoptera frugiperda, researchers identified two new PIWI genes conserved in Spodoptera, annotated piRNA clusters in both strains, and found strain-specific transposon targeting—possibly linked to reproductive isolation. A piRNA cluster within the masc gene suggests piRNAs also regulate sex determination in this major invasive pest.

papers.title: CRISPR-dCas9 epigenetic reprogramming in cancer: platforms, immuno-modulation and delivery challenges.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes 2015–2025 literature on CRISPR-dCas9 epigenetic editing in cancer: multi-effector platforms amplifying chromatin modifications, precision enhancer-targeting systems (enCRISPRa/i), immunotherapeutic strategies upregulating NK/T-cell ligands and MHC genes in tumor cells, and next-generation delivery approaches. Remaining barriers to clinical translation include off-target effects and context-dependence of editing outcomes.

papers.title: Hirudin suppresses ovarian cancer cell proliferation and glycolysis through inhibiting the NF-κB/HK3 axis.
papers.summary: Hirudin inhibited ovarian cancer cell proliferation, migration, and invasion dose-dependently. Network pharmacology and dual-luciferase assays identified NF-κB as a key target: hirudin suppressed NF-κB-driven hexokinase 3 expression, reducing glycolysis, extracellular acidification, and oxygen consumption. The work positions hirudin as a candidate metabolism-targeted therapy and a route past chemoresistance.
